records.title: Environment and Society: Understanding Issues, Finding Solutions
records.header: ENVIR 100 Environment and Society: Understanding Issues, Finding Solutions (5) SSc/NSc, DIV
records.text: ENVIR 100 Environment and Society: Understanding Issues, Finding Solutions (5) SSc/NSc, DIV Examines the ethical, political, social, and scientific dimensions of environmental issues. Integrates knowledge from different disciplines while evaluating environmental problems at various scales. Uses an environmental justice lens to examine the ways problems are concentrated in some communities while providing opportunities to practice environmental communication and collaboration across disciplines. Course overlaps with: TESC 220. Offered: AWSpS.

records.text: ENVIR 101 Orientation to Environmental Studies (1) Introduction to the Environmental Studies program and learning community. Weekly group discussions focus on majoring in and pursuing a career in Environmental Studies. Topics include philosophy and structure of the Program on the Environment, connecting academic work to career pursuits, undergraduate research, networking, and connecting with peers and faculty at UW. Credit/no-credit only.

records.text: ENVIR 103 Society and the Oceans (5) NSc/SSc, DIV Explores the social, justice, and policy dimensions of the ocean environment and ocean management policy. records.header: ENVIR 200 Sustainability and Environmental Justice (5) SSc, DIV
records.text: ENVIR 200 Sustainability and Environmental Justice (5) SSc, DIV Uses interdisciplinary approach to explore intersections of sustainability and environmental justice, analyze social-environmental challenges, and develop equitable responses. Investigates ways that attempts to improve sustainability can exacerbate existing inequalities. Critically evaluates synergies and tensions between sustainability and justice, and considers how different perspectives inform pathways toward a more just and sustainable future Offered: AWSp.

records.title: Climate Governance: How Individuals, Communities, NGOs, Firms, and Governments Can Solve the Climate Crisis
records.header: ENVIR 201 Climate Governance: How Individuals, Communities, NGOs, Firms, and Governments Can Solve the Climate Crisis (5) SSc/NSc, DIV
records.text: ENVIR 201 Climate Governance: How Individuals, Communities, NGOs, Firms, and Governments Can Solve the Climate Crisis (5) SSc/NSc, DIV Examines climate change, its causes and impacts (on ecosystems, water availability, extreme weather, communities, health, and food) globally, nationally, and locally. Surveys its solutions (mitigation, adaptation, migration, and just transition), actors that implement them (governments, firms, NGOs, activists, communities, individuals) and approaches they use (regulation, markets, planning, innovation, social movements, behavioral change). Offered: jointly with SMEA 201; Sp.

records.header: ENVIR 210 Food and the Environment (5) SSc/NSc
records.text: ENVIR 210 Food and the Environment (5) SSc/NSc Relates the production and consumption of food to the major areas of environmental science including energy use, water consumption, biodiversity loss, soil loss, pollution, nutrient cycles, and climate change. Studies the basic science and how food production impacts the key processes.

records.title: Environmental Justice
records.header: ENVIR 211 Environmental Justice (5) SSc, DIV
records.text: ENVIR 211 Environmental Justice (5) SSc, DIV Examines introductory studies of environmental racism and ecological injustice in the United States and select areas of the world. Reviews environmental justice theories and methods applied to risk science, ecosystem management, biodiversity conservation, and sustainable development. Includes comparative studies of social movements for "eco-justice." Offered: jointly with AES 211/ANTH 211.

records.title: Global Environmental Justice
records.header: ENVIR 212 Global Environmental Justice (5) SSc, DIV
records.text: ENVIR 212 Global Environmental Justice (5) SSc, DIV Examines why environmental disasters (such as floods, fires, and oil spills) hit some countries harder than others. Explores global environmental justice, examining how political, economic, and social systems distribute environmental harm unevenly. Uses tools and frameworks to challenge these inequalities and explores recent events like heatwaves and wildfires through an environmental justice lens. Course overlaps with: HSTAA 208. Offered: jointly with JSIS B 212.

records.header: ENVIR 221 US Environmental History: Ecology, Culture, Justice (5) SSc
records.text: ENVIR 221 US Environmental History: Ecology, Culture, Justice (5) SSc Covers the intertwined history of the environment and American society, focusing on issues of inequality and justice. Topics include colonialism, capitalist expansion, chemical and nuclear industrialism, the environmental inequalities of cities and suburbs, environmental movements, and environmental justice. Offered: jointly with HSTAA 221; A.

records.text: ENVIR 235 Introduction to Environmental Economics (5) SSc/NSc Introduces environmental and natural resource economics. Discusses fundamental economic concepts, including markets and private property. records.text: ENVIR 239 Sustainability: Personal Choices, Broad Impacts (5) NSc/SSc Introduces implications of and approaches to sustainability through models of sustainability, history of sustainability movements, and sustainability in action. records.text: ENVIR 308 American Indians and the Environment (5) SSc, DIV Examines the historical relationships American Indians have possessed with local environments, with special attention to the ways these peoples have adapted to altered environments and new conditions, including migrations, involvement with markets of exchange, overhunting, dispossession, conservation, and mainstream environmentalism. records.header: ENVIR 310 Data Analysis in Environmental Studies (5) NSc, RSN
records.text: ENVIR 310 Data Analysis in Environmental Studies (5) NSc, RSN Practical data-analysis workshop that introduces analysis of quantitative and qualitative data from social and environmental topics. Students use public data or research data to develop skills in data organization, visualization, and statistics. Students evaluate the use of socio-environmental data in graphics and learn to use data to make informed decisions. Quantitative methods, qualitative analysis, and survey analysis are introduced. Recommended: either ENVIR 301 or equivalent introductory course on research methods and data collection. Offered: SpS.

records.header: ENVIR 312 Food System Sustainability and Resilience (3) NSc/SSc
records.text: ENVIR 312 Food System Sustainability and Resilience (3) NSc/SSc Explores concepts of sustainability and resilience as used today in the study and management of food production systems. Emphasizes a systems-thinking approach to assessing current and future challenges and resilience in the face of stresses and shocks. Covers complex dynamics between biological and geophysical aspects of food production systems in the context of nourishing a growing population, evaluation of co-benefits and tradeoffs. Recommended: introductory coursework in food systems or sustainability. Offered: jointly with NUTR 312; Sp.

Models of "green development"; ways in which norms for resource use have entered global politics. Patterns of state compliance with international environmental agreements, and why states fall short of meeting their international obligations. Offered: jointly with JSIS B 350/SCAND 350.

records.text: ENVIR 371 Anthropology of Development (5) SSc Development refers to social, economic, cultural, political transformations viewed as progress. Studied from anthropological perspectives. records.header: ENVIR 379 Environmental Sociology (5) NSc/SSc
records.text: ENVIR 379 Environmental Sociology (5) NSc/SSc Focuses on interrelations between the natural environment, social systems, and human behavior. Covers foundational and contemporary sociological and social-psychological theories and approaches used to examine the social construction of nature; environmental risk, hazards, and disasters; the climate crisis; environmental inequality and racism; consumption and corporate environmental responsibility; and Indigenous environmental justice. Prerequisite: ESRM 200 or ENVIR 100. Offered: jointly with ESRM 371/SOC 379; W.

records.header: ENVIR 380 Wilderness in the Anthropocene (5) SSc, DIV
records.text: ENVIR 380 Wilderness in the Anthropocene (5) SSc, DIV Explores the ways in which landscapes change over time while considering wilderness as a space and an idea. Who benefits and who is marginalized from wilderness? How does wilderness serve humans ecologically and psychologically? How and by whom should wilderness be managed for equitable, ethical, and sustainable outcomes for nature and people? Includes pre-trip readings, lecture, and discussion, up to two weeks in field, and post-trip writing. Offered: S.

records.title: Climate Justice at Universities
records.header: ENVIR 435 Climate Justice at Universities (5) SSc, DIV
records.text: ENVIR 435 Climate Justice at Universities (5) SSc, DIV Explores the role and responsibility of universities in struggles for climate justice. Examines how universities were influenced by racialized and gendered oppression, environmental exploitation, and colonial intervention. Focuses on three areas of university life: the campus, student body, and research. Topics include divestment from fossil fuels, campus infrastructure, and social movements. Offered: jointly with JSIS B 435.

records.title: Attaining a Sustainable Society
records.header: ENVIR 439 Attaining a Sustainable Society (5) SSc/NSc, DIV
records.text: ENVIR 439 Attaining a Sustainable Society (5) SSc/NSc, DIV Building a sustainable future requires restructuring the global economy and changes in values and lifestyles. How do race, culture, gender, class, and individual experience inform sustainability priorities? How do internalized notions of power and success compliment or undermine our societal efforts towards sustainability? Students explore these questions through four arenas for change: food, governance, economics, and energy. Offered: W.

The political-economic dimensions of ecological change. Contemporary environmental movements including the varieties of bioregionalism, deep ecology, ecofeminism, ecosocialism, environmental justice, and social ecology. Offered: jointly with ANTH 459.

records.text: ENVIR 460 Power, Privilege, and Preservation (5) SSc, DIV Critically examines strategies of resource managers to integrate local communities and cultures in protected areas management. Explores issues of power, privilege, and injustice and their impacts on individuals, society, and resource management decisions. Examines the potential for more socially just and ecologically sustainable approaches to protected areas management. Offered: jointly with ESRM 460; ASpS.

records.title: Climate Justice
records.header: ENVIR 466 Climate Justice (4) SSc, DIV
records.text: ENVIR 466 Climate Justice (4) SSc, DIV Covers human dimensions of climate change and variability, focusing on analyzing relationships between physical climate risks and systemic marginalization. Examines how climate impacts are unevenly distributed and experienced, critical appraisal of dominant climate action movements, and learning from underrepresented scholars, communities, and activists advancing transformative social and political reorganization for (climate) justice. records.text: ENVIR 480 Sustainability Consulting Practicum (5, max. 10) Explores sustainability on the UW campus, in local businesses, and in Seattle communities while providing opportunities to learn about project design, management, and consulting. records.title: Environmental Studies Capstone: Preparation
records.header: ENVIR 490 Environmental Studies Capstone: Preparation (5)
records.text: ENVIR 490 Environmental Studies Capstone: Preparation (5) Engage with representatives of established research projects and internship programs to design a capstone project and secure a related internship. Articulate connections between proposed capstone project and larger social-environmental issues and scholarly questions. Participate in professional development activities, complete a project learning contract and a research proposal. First in a series of three. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 2.0 in ENVIR 301; a minimum grade of 2.0 in ENVIR 302; and a minimum grade of 2.0 in ENVIR 401. Offered: ASp.
